story: Alex stared at the blinking cursor, his chest tightening into a hard, unyielding knot that made every shallow breath feel like a struggle against invisible weights. The deadline had passed hours ago, yet he remained frozen, his fingers hovering over the keys as if touching them would shatter the fragile illusion of control he had clung to all week. Sweat trickled down his spine, cold and clammy, while the silence of the empty apartment pressed against his ears with a deafening intensity that drowned out his own racing thoughts. He wanted to scream, to break the monitor, to run until his lungs burned, but his limbs felt heavy and disconnected, as though they belonged to someone else entirely.

Alex stared at the blinking cursor on the blank screen, his fingers trembling slightly as they hovered over the keyboard. The clock ticked loudly, each second stretching into an eternity that pressed heavily against his chest, making it difficult to breathe. He had already sent three emails to the bank, his voice cracking on the last call, but the silence from their end was deafening and absolute. A cold sweat prickled along his hairline, mixing with the stale coffee that had gone cold hours ago on his desk. He rubbed his eyes until stars danced in his vision, knowing that tomorrow would bring eviction notices if he did not find a solution right now.

Alex stared at the blinking cursor on the screen, his fingers hovering over the keyboard like trapped birds. The silence in the apartment grew heavy, pressing against his eardrums until a low hum replaced the ticking clock. He had sent forty-seven emails that day, each one a carefully crafted plea for recognition that vanished into the digital void without a trace. His chest tightened, a physical weight that made every shallow breath feel like a struggle against an invisible tide. He deleted the draft again, watching the words disappear, knowing he had no other options left to explore. The sun dipped below the horizon, casting long, dark shadows across his desk, mirroring the void inside him.
